analysis.title: King Apple winning the AI race by not running
key_insights: Apple is the only Magnificent Seven stock outperforming both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 year-to-date, up 25% YTD, and has recently decoupled from the Nasdaq.
Since 2023 the four major hyperscalers have increased capex roughly 6-9x, while Apple's capex is below pre-AI-boom levels.
As a share of sales, hyperscaler capex has doubled or tripled, while Apple's has fallen by roughly a third.
Apple trades at roughly 36x forward earnings, a 17-turn premium to the S&P 500, described as a record relative valuation.
57% of analysts rate Apple buy/overweight, versus more than 90% for NVDA at its peak.
The Market Ear's long Apple anti-AI trade continues to perform. Apple is beating the NDX, and the trade expressed against NVDA is doing even better.

market_movers.rationale: Apple is outperforming the Magnificent Seven and the Nasdaq 100 while keeping capex flat. The Market Ear's long Apple anti-AI trade continues to work.

trade_ideas.description: Long AAPL anti-AI trade, outright versus the NDX and expressed as long AAPL vs NVDA
trade_ideas.rationale: Apple is outperforming the NDX by not spending on AI capex, and the pair against NVDA is performing even better.

risk_factors: Apple trades at a record relative valuation premium of about 17 turns to the S&P 500.
charts_described: Chart shows Apple up 25% YTD, the only Magnificent Seven stock ahead of both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100.
Chart indexed to Q1 2023 shows Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon capex rising sharply while Apple's has barely moved.
Chart shows Apple at roughly 36x forward earnings, a 17-turn premium to the S&P 500.
vol_and_positioning: Apple has decoupled from the Nasdaq and trades at a record relative valuation premium of about 17 turns over the S&P 500 (roughly 36x forward earnings).
Only 57% of analysts are buy/overweight on Apple, versus more than 90% for NVDA at its peak.
